description: Replace the linear learning rate warmdown with a cosine decay to provide a smoother transition to the final learning rate.
Reduce Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 3 in Muon optimizer to save wall-clock time.
Zero-init output projections: no edit, because the incumbent already zero-initializes both attn.c_proj and mlp.c_proj in init_weights.

Mix each later layer's value projection with the first layer's value projection using a learned per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5, adding only a few scalar parameters that get their own small-LR Adam group.
Add gradient norm clipping before optimizer step to stabilize training at high learning rates
Apply decaying weight decay to Muon optimizer using the remaining learning rate fraction.
Add Z-loss regularization on output logits to stabilize logit scale and reduce val_bpb.

issues: (1) Evaluation path altered: the z-loss is added inside GPT.forward, which the evaluation also calls (with reduction='none' to get per-token losses). The value returned to the evaluator is no longer pure cross-entropy: it is CE plus 1e-4 * mean(lse^2). That scalar is broadcast onto every per-token loss, so the measured val_bpb is biased. The bias is upward, so it doesn't flatter the candidate, but the measured quantity has still been changed. The harness's integrity flag is justified.

(2) Semantics bug: z_loss ignores reduction and ignore_index=-1. It averages over every position, including masked targets, and with reduction='none' it adds the same batch-level scalar to each token. Any per-token or bpb number computed from this forward is therefore wrong.

Fix: apply the z-loss only during training. Either compute it in the training loop from the logits, or add it only when self.training and reduction=='mean', masking positions where targets==-1. Return plain CE in every other case. As a regularizer it is legitimate.
(3) There are no harness numbers because the run was rejected, so z cannot be recomputed. The comment's claim that this gives 'low val_bpb' is unsupported.
Minor: the diff also removes a blank line before the optimizer section. This is cosmetic.

description: The crash came from the z-loss term in GPT.forward: lse is a per-token vector, so z_loss stayed non-scalar and loss.backward() failed; averaging z_loss over tokens makes the total loss scalar again.
Increase depth from 8 to 10 layers and lower ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 51 so model_dim stays at 512 (4 heads of 128), giving a deeper model at roughly the incumbent's matrix-parameter cost.
Replace the linear learning rate warmdown with a sqrt-shaped warmdown to decay the learning rate more slowly at first and faster near the end.
Implement linear layer-wise learning rate scaling for matrix parameters using a layer_inherited parameter
Halve HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so the 512-dim model gets 8 attention heads of width 64 instead of 4 heads of width 128, with everything else unchanged.
Setting Adam's beta1 to 0.9 for embedding, scalar, unembedding parameters to test smoother first-moment estimation.
Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to increase optimizer step frequency within the time budget.

Sequence length curriculum: for the first 50% of the time budget, reshape each micro-batch from (64, 2048) to (128, 1024) so tokens per step stay constant, then switch to full 2048 context for the remaining training.
Implement separate warmdown schedules for Adam groups (earlier start at 0.3 progress) and Muon matrix parameters (standard 0.5 warmdown).
The logging print references an undefined variable `lrm`, so I replaced it with the muon LR multiplier that is already computed as `multipliers['muon']`.
Keep an EMA (decay 0.999) of the raw model parameters, updated after each optimizer step, and swap those EMA weights in just before the final evaluation call.
Abort QK normalization: train.py already RMS-normalizes q and k per head after rotary embedding (q, k = norm(q), norm(k)), so the spec is already implemented.

Use grouped-query attention with half as many KV heads (n_kv_head = n_head // 2), repeating each K/V head across its paired query heads with repeat_interleave before rotary and attention so the attention call and shapes are unchanged.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call or the final summary printing.
There are no numbers yet because no GPU run has happened. There is nothing to check claims against, so z cannot be recomputed.

Risk to check: the MTP flag is set once per step, before the step runs. The eval only stays correct if use_mtp is False when evaluation starts. That holds while WARMDOWN_RATIO > 0, because training ends after the warmdown starts and the flag is off by then. If WARMDOWN_RATIO is ever 0, the flag stays True at eval. With reduction='none', loss is B*T long and loss2 is B*(T-1) long, so the eval would crash on the shape mismatch or be corrupted. A guard such as `raw_model.use_mtp = False` before eval, outside the eval code, would be safer. Flagged, not vetoed.

Turning use_mtp on and off on a model compiled with dynamic=False triggers at least one recompile at the start of the warmdown. That recompile happens inside the timed loop and uses some of the 300 s budget. It is a small cost, not a validity problem.

mtp_adapter is an n_embd x n_embd matrix in the lm_head AdamW group. It is counted in the parameter and FLOP reporting but is not used once the auxiliary loss turns off in the warmdown. This is a minor cosmetic point.
The auxiliary loss shares lm_head, so loss2 also sends gradients into the main head. That is intended. Whether 0.1 is a good weight is an empirical question, not a bug.

description: Add a t+2 auxiliary prediction head (shared lm_head, zero-initialized residual linear adapter) with loss weight 0.1 during training, switched off from the start of warmdown, leaving the t+1 eval path unchanged.
Apply label smoothing regularization to training loss by mixing targets with uniform distribution, which can reduce overconfidence and val_bpb.

Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU block (gate and up projections to a hidden width of about 8/3 * model_dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, then silu(gate) * up and a down projection), keeping the parameter count close to baseline; the new matrices fall into the existing Muon shape groups automatically.
